annotations.title: You may haue ſocietie.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> S. Iohn ſheweth manifeſtly, that vvhoſoeuer deſire to be partakers with God, muſt firſt be vnited to the Churches ſocietie, learne that faith, and receiue thoſe Sacraments, which the Diſciples receiued of the Truth it ſelf, conuerſant with them in fleſh. So ſaith Venerable Bede vpon this place. Vvhereby we ſee there is no ſocietie vvith God in ſectes or ſchiſmes, nor any where but in the vnitie, fellowſhip, and communion of that Church which can proue it ſelf to deſcend from the Apoſtles.

notes.text: No saluation but in the Societie of the Church.

annotations.title: The bloud of Ieſvs.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> Whether ſinnes be remitted by praiers, by faſting, by almes, by faith, by charitie, by ſacrifice, by Sacraments, & by the Prieſts, (as the holy Scriptures do plainely attribute remiſſion to euery of theſe) yet none of al theſe do othervviſe remit, but in the force, by the merite & vertue of Chriſts bloud: theſe being but the appointed meanes & inſtruments by vvhich Chriſt wil haue his holy bloud to worke effectually in vs. vvhich meanes whoſoeuer contemneth, depriueth him ſelf of the comoditie of Chriſts ovvne bloud, & continueth ſtill in ſinne and vncleanneſſe, vaunt he him ſelf neuer ſo much of Chriſts death. Vvhich point let the Proteſtants marke wel, and ceaſe to beguile their poore deceiued folowers, perſuading them, that the Catholikes derogate from Chriſts bloud, or ſeeke remiſſion othervviſe then by it, for that they vſe humbly the meanes appointed by Chriſt to apply the benefite of his holy bloud vnto them.

notes.text: Many meanes & instruments of remitting sinne, but al by the force & merite of Christs bloud applied by them.

annotations.title: From al ſinne.
annotations.text: ◦ From original and actual, venial and mortal, a culpa & pœna, that is, from the fault and the paine due for the ſame. V. Bede ſaith, that Chriſts Paſſion doth not onely remit in Baptiſme the ſinnes before committed. but al other afterward alſo done by frailtie: yet ſo, if vve vſe for the remiſſion of them, ſuch meanes as be requiſite and as Chriſt hath appointed, whereof he reckeneth ſome. Bede vpon this place. See S. Auguſtine alſo vpon this place to. 9. and S. Hierome li. 2 con. Pelag. c. 3.

notes.text: Al remission of sinnes is by the Passion of Christ, though by secundarie meanes also.

annotations.title: That we haue no ſinne.
annotations.text: [1] We gather by theſe wordes and the former, that there be two ſortes of ſinnes: one mortal, excluding vs from light and the ſocietie of God: an other venial, which is found euen in thoſe that walke in the light, and are in the ſocietie of God. [2] Alſo we note againſt the Pelagians, that we be truely called the ſonnes of God, and ſo iuſt in deede, though vve be not without al ſinnes, euery one of vs, as wel iuſt as vniuſt, being taught and bound to confeſſe our offenſes, and to aſke pardon daily of God, by this petition of the Pater noſter, Forgiue vs our debtes. Therfore S. Auguſtine li. de natura & grat. c. 36. reckeneth vp al the holy Patriarches, Prophets, and renovvmed iuſt perſons, to haue been ſinners, euen vvhen they vvere in grace and iuſtice: [3] excepting alwaies our B. Ladie, de qua propter honorem Domini, nullam prorſus, cùm de peccatis agitur, habere volo quæſtionem. of whom, ſaith he, for the honour of our Lord, when we talke of ſinnes, I wil haue no queſtion. And Pelagius aſking what ſinnes Abel & ſuch iuſt men did commit, [4] [5] S. Auguſtine anſwereth, that they might laugh ſometime immoderately, or ieſt to much, or couet ſomewhat intemperatly, or plucke fruite ouer greedily, or in eating take ſomewhat more then afterward was wel digeſted, or haue their intention in time of praier ſomewhat diſtracted, and ſuch like. thus in ſenſe S. Auguſtine. Whereby we may learne which be venial ſinnes, that conſiſt vvith true iuſtice & [6] can not alwaies be auoided euen of holy men in this life. In the booke de fide ad Petrum c. 41. are excepted from this common rule of ſinners, the children which be newely baptized and haue not yet vſe of reaſon to ſinne either mortally or venially.

notes.text: A man may be truely iust, notwithstanding venial sinnes.
S. Augustine excepteth our B. Ladie from sinners.
